shared: The Celerity is a fifteen-ton ultralight quadrupedal drone BattleMech originally conceived by ComStar's advanced research division in 3052. Born from the drone warfare experiments that followed the Battle of Tukayyid, the design represents an extreme approach to expendable reconnaissance, a four-legged chassis stripped to its mechanical essentials and controlled remotely from a modified Fury combat vehicle hub. The Republic of the Sphere later adopted the concept following the activation of the Fortress Protocols, creating a true OmniMech version from 3138 onward. Capable of speeds rivaling the fastest VTOLs in existence, the Celerity has served as a swift and disposable instrument of reconnaissance, electronic interdiction, and even direct combat.

The Celerity's defining characteristic is its extraordinary speed. A Republic 240-rated XXL fusion engine propels the fifteen-ton quadruped to cruising speeds of one hundred seventy-two kilometers per hour, with MASC pushing its maximum sprint to nearly three hundred forty-six kilometers per hour, performance that matches or exceeds most VTOLs and conventional aircraft on approach. This speed comes at severe cost: the design carries barely a ton and a half of Strasbourg Armaments Type 3 armor, rendering it catastrophically vulnerable to even glancing hits. The fragile XXL engine and XL gyro compound this vulnerability, as even a minor stumble at full speed could cripple the chassis.

The OmniMech version carries two tons of pod space, a modest allocation that nonetheless enables a surprising range of mission profiles. Configurations span from electronic warfare and sensor operations to direct-fire interdiction with Clan-specification weapons. The S-Equus Omicron endo steel frame provides structural efficiency while the ComStar Remote Link Theta communications system maintains the critical drone control link. RAF engineers equipped the OmniMech version with double heat sinks to support energy-intensive configurations, a practical enhancement over the original C3i-equipped prototype. The quadrupedal layout provides inherently stable footing at high speeds, though the consequences of any terrain misstep remain dire given the chassis's minimal protection.

ComStar's drone warfare program began in earnest following the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052. The initial concept relied on existing platforms, swift hovercraft and VTOLs controlled remotely from modified Fury combat vehicles, but the program's ambitions quickly outpaced available technology. Under the guidance of Precentor Ashok Sethi, engineers pursued an increasingly radical approach, designing a purpose-built ultralight four-legged BattleMech frame optimized exclusively for drone operations. The resulting CLR-02-X-D prototype represented an extreme engineering exercise: a fifteen-ton quadruped built around an oversized engine, equipped with a C3i module and full-head ejection system to protect the expensive electronics in its expendable airframe.

Prototypes were produced in limited numbers, but the design never achieved full production under ComStar. The Jihad disrupted the program, and the Word of Blake's dissolution scattered much of the underlying research. ComStar's surviving remnants maintained a small cadre of operational Celeritys, most of which were destroyed during the Blessed Order's desperate last stand against the Republic of the Sphere at Epsilon Eridani in 3141.

The Republic's subsequent adoption of the Celerity represented a resurrection of long-abandoned technology. Following the activation of the Fortress Protocols, the RAF Manufacturing Center Providence on Terra began producing a true OmniMech version designated the CLR-03-O from approximately 3138. RAF engineers refined the original concept into a more versatile platform, and Stone's Fury became an early adopter, experimenting with packs of Celerity drones across the towns and villages of Liberty. The machines were carefully disguised to appear as pre-Republic ComStar units, creating deliberate confusion about their origin.

Reports of Celerity sightings in the Ghost Bear Dominion, the Draconis Combine, and the Capellan Confederation during this period generated considerable alarm, as intelligence analysts struggled to identify who was deploying these ultralight drones and to what purpose. Local intercepts indicated contacts with Word of Blake remnants, pirates, and even Homeworld Clan advance scouts, though the true source remained the Republic operating from behind the walls of Fortress Republic. The danger of discovery was deemed an acceptable risk given the strategic intelligence these expendable assets provided. The Celerity has since appeared in the Solaris VII arena circuit as a remote-controlled combat drone, suggesting that the concept of expendable drone warfare may be poised to enter a new era of development.

The Centurion OmniMech was introduced by Corean Enterprises in the second decade of the thirty-second century as part of the company's effort to expand its market share. Manufactured at Corean's facility on New Avalon and designated the CN11-O, this fifty-ton OmniMech draws heavily on the legacy of the original Centurion BattleMech that served the Federated Suns for centuries. The design was a natural evolution for Corean, whose experience with countless Centurion upgrades and the advanced Legionnaire made the classic chassis an ideal candidate for OmniMech conversion.

Built on a Corean Model OM77 endo steel frame with a Magna 250 XL engine and compact gyro, the CN11-O achieves a top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour while dedicating twenty-four tons (nearly half its total mass) to pod space. The most common configurations deliberately echo the varied weapon loadouts that Centurion variants have carried over the centuries, providing MechWarriors with familiar tactical options in a flexible, reconfigurable package.

The Centurion OmniMech's design philosophy centers on versatility through reconfiguration. The fixed chassis mounts a Magna 250 XL engine, ten double heat sinks, and nine and a half tons of StarGuard III standard armor on a Corean Model OM77 endo steel frame fitted with a compact gyro. This combination provides twenty-four tons of available pod space, offering exceptional flexibility for a medium OmniMech and allowing field commanders to tailor each machine to the demands of a specific mission.

The Primary configuration echoes the proven CN9-D loadout, mounting an LB 10-X autocannon, an Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-10, and two extended-range medium lasers with CASE II-protected ammunition stores. Across all six standard configurations, the Centurion OmniMech maintains the traditional emphasis on combining long and short range weaponry, with loadouts available for roles ranging from precision sniping to close-quarters melee combat. A noted deficiency is that only two of the six standard configurations mount jump jets, an increasingly important tactical tool on the modern battlefield.

The Centurion OmniMech entered service during a period when Corean Enterprises sought to expand beyond its traditional Centurion lineup. The company's centuries of experience with the platform, including the development of the advanced Legionnaire, made the Centurion a natural candidate for OmniMech conversion. The CN11-O's introduction in the 3110s coincided with the design largely dominating New Avalon's Centurion production output, contributing to the decline of the older CN10 line.

In the field, the Centurion OmniMech has seen service primarily with Federated Suns commands along the Draconis March. Units of the Morrill Draconis March Militia developed a notable tactical innovation, pairing traditional BattleMech Centurions with OmniMech variants in mixed formations. During engagements with Wolf's Dragoons striker battalions conducting spoiling raids from the Combine, the militia exploited the OmniMech's reconfiguration capability to deceive their opponents. By swapping configurations between attacks, the mixed Centurion formations convinced the Dragoons that the Morrill DMM had been heavily reinforced, causing them to abandon their advance and retreat off-world rather than press the attack.

By 3145, the Centurion OmniMech had established itself as a reliable utility platform within the AFFS, with its six standard configurations offering sufficient tactical variety to fulfill the diverse roles that Centurion variants have traditionally served throughout the design's storied service history.

text.overview:
The Cataphract is a seventy-ton heavy BattleMech introduced in 3025 by the Capellan Confederation, representing one of the first entirely new designs produced during the Succession Wars. Designed by Earthwerks Incorporated on Tikonov, the Cataphract was born from desperation, assembled from components adapted from existing designs including the Marauder, Shadow Hawk, and Phoenix Hawk. Nicknamed a "FrankenMech" for its ungainly appearance, the design nonetheless proved functional and capable of sustained production with the Confederation's limited industrial capacity.

What should have been one of House Liao's proudest achievements instead became a symbol of humiliation when the Tikonov factories fell to House Davion during the Fourth Succession War in 3029. Both successor states subsequently developed the chassis in divergent directions, with the Federated Commonwealth pursuing ballistic-focused upgrades while the Capellans emphasized energy weapons and electronic warfare capabilities from their replacement facility on Grand Base.
text.capabilities:
The original CTF-1X Cataphract carries a CeresArms Smasher PPC as its primary long-range weapon, complemented by a SarLon MaxiCannon autocannon/10 that provides reliable medium-range firepower. Four CeresArms medium lasers distributed across the torso and arms deliver substantial close-range punch, giving the design effective engagement options at multiple range brackets. Powered by a standard VOX 280 fusion engine, the Cataphract moves at a maximum speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, adequate for its intended role as a frontline combatant but unremarkable among heavy 'Mechs.

The Cataphract's design philosophy prioritizes manufacturability over elegance. The mixed heritage of its components means replacement parts can be sourced from multiple production lines, a critical advantage for the resource-starved Confederation. Thirteen tons of Kallon Royalstar armor provide respectable protection for its weight class, though the design lacks jump jets, limiting its tactical flexibility in rough terrain. Heat management requires discipline from the pilot, as sustained fire from the full weapons suite can overwhelm the fourteen heat sinks.

Despite these compromises, the Cataphract delivers a reliable combination of firepower and durability that has kept it in frontline service across multiple centuries and successor states, proof of the soundness of the original engineering despite its cobbled-together origins.
text.deployment: This variant is a common field variant of the CTF-5L that trades the variable-speed pulse lasers and two heat sinks for four jump jets and two standard medium lasers. This conversion transforms the design into a potent skirmisher, combining the 5L's reflective armor and heavy long-range armament with the tactical mobility that many Cataphract variants have historically lacked. The jump capability allows this variant to exploit terrain advantages and reposition rapidly, making it a more versatile combatant than its parent variant despite the modest reduction in close-range energy firepower.
text.battleHistory:
The Cataphract's origins lie in the final years of the Third Succession War, when the Capellan Confederation found itself desperately short of heavy BattleMechs. The loss of the Carver V factories to the Free Worlds League in 2953 stripped the nation of vital heavy and assault 'Mech production capacity. Earthwerks Incorporated on Tikonov began Cataphract production in 3025, assembling the design from available components in a feat of pragmatic engineering. The left arm was originally a right arm from a Shadow Hawk, the legs and torso drew from the Marauder, and Phoenix Hawk components rounded out the design. The result was far from aesthetically pleasing, but it was both functional and (critically) something the Confederation could actually build.

The Cataphract had barely entered limited service when the Fourth Succession War erupted, and the fall of Tikonov to the Seventh Crucis Lancers in 3029 transferred the entire production line to the Federated Suns. The conquering Davion forces embraced the captured design, though production quality suffered due to deliberate sabotage by workers still loyal to the Confederation. Many commands that participated in Operation Rat rebuilt using captured equipment, and the Cataphract became a common sight in the Crucis Lancers. The appearance of a distinctly Capellan BattleMech in Davion service caused considerable confusion among Kurita troops during fighting on the Draconis frontier in 3039.

Chancellor Romano Liao directed the establishment of a replacement Cataphract production facility on Grand Base, with the line operational by 3032 in time to deploy units against the Andurien invaders. When the St. Ives Compact broke away from the Confederation, a number of prototype Cataphracts fell under the control of the St. Ives Lancers, further dispersing the design across the Inner Sphere.

The Clan Invasion of 3049 drove both nations to upgrade the design aggressively. The Federated Commonwealth developed the CTF-3D at Tikonov, mounting an extra-light engine and advanced autocannons to create a more versatile platform. Despite the improvements, the 3D saw only marginal deployment with the AFFC and was eventually relegated to the Crucis March Militia. The Capellans, having stolen the 3D's plans, produced their own variant at Grand Base, the CTF-3L, which constituted a remarkable twenty-five percent of all newly acquired Capellan heavy 'Mechs during the 3050s.

The Xin Sheng movement and the recapture of Tikonov brought renewed Capellan investment in the design. Sun Tzu Liao ordered the 3D line retooled for the stealth-armored CTF-4L, intended for the growing number of Shadow Lances within the CCAF, though sabotage of the engine production line delayed full production until 3070. During the Jihad, Johnston Industries on New Syrtis leveraged battlefield salvage to produce the CTF-5D, while factory ownership across Tikonov changed hands multiple times as the Word of Blake, Republic of the Sphere, and eventually the Federated Suns and Capellan Confederation each claimed the world.

The Cataphract continued to evolve into the Dark Age and ilClan eras. The CTF-5L incorporated reflective armor and shared components with the newly redesigned Thunderbolt, while its jump-capable CTF-5LL variant proved a potent skirmisher. More than a century after its inauspicious debut as a FrankenMech cobbled together from spare parts, the Cataphract remained a mainstay of Capellan and former Federated Suns arsenals alike.

text.overview:
The Catapult is a 65-ton fire-support BattleMech first manufactured in 2561 by Hollis Incorporated, a Terran Hegemony defense firm. Designed in anticipation of the Reunification War, the Catapult filled the role of a second-line missile platform capable of punishing enemies at extreme range while maintaining enough mobility to reposition across broken terrain. Hollis produced the chassis in substantial numbers during its initial contract, though the Hegemony deemed the design adequate rather than exceptional and declined to renew the agreement.

Produced across multiple manufacturing runs spanning the late Age of War through the Succession Wars era, the Catapult has remained one of the Inner Sphere's most recognizable heavy BattleMech silhouettes. Its distinctive pod-mounted launchers and armless profile have made it an enduring symbol of indirect fire doctrine, and the chassis has proven remarkably adaptable to a wide range of combat roles well beyond its original missile-support mission.
text.capabilities:
The Catapult is primarily a fire-support platform built around a pair of Holly Long Range Missile 15-rack launchers mounted in distinctive pod-like housings flanking the cockpit. These thirty-tube launchers can begin engaging targets at ranges exceeding 600 meters, well before most opponents can effectively respond. When enemies close within the missiles' minimum effective range, four Martell medium lasers mounted below the cockpit provide adequate short-range defense capable of discouraging most light and medium 'Mechs from pressing an engagement. The design's greatest vulnerability lies in its ammunition dependency, carrying only eight reloads per launcher, which makes the Catapult heavily reliant on logistical support during extended operations.

Ten tons of Durallex Heavy armor provides respectable protection for a fire-support platform, while the Magna 260 fusion engine drives the chassis to a maximum speed of 64 kilometers per hour. Four jump jets grant a 120-meter jumping capability that allows the Catapult to keep pace with faster units across broken terrain. Early production jump jets proved prone to breakdowns that vented heat directly into the 'Mech's interior, a flaw that was addressed in later models but never fully eliminated from all operational units. The lack of arms limits close-quarters capability and leaves the design without anti-infantry weapons, reinforcing the need to maintain standoff distance whenever possible. A distinctive sideways ejection system, while generally considered safe, has been known to surprise pilots unfamiliar with the design.
text.deployment: This custom configuration emerged from the uneven supply conditions of the early Clan Invasion, creating a unique patchwork variant that combined new and old components. The standard PPCs were replaced with Extended Range models, and the heat sinks were upgraded to double-strength units to better manage the increased thermal load. The machine guns were removed to restore the C1's original jump jet configuration, returning the mobility that the standard K2 had sacrificed. The result was a more mobile and harder-hitting variant of the K2 that reflected the improvisation demanded by wartime logistics.
text.battleHistory:
The Catapult's operational history spans centuries of continuous service across the Inner Sphere. Hollis Incorporated was originally a Terran Hegemony company whose first production run of the Catapult predated the colonization of Corey and the formation of the Star League by nearly a decade. During the Star League era, the design served primarily with second-line and specialist formations, including mountaineering regiments that exploited its jump capability in difficult terrain. When Hollis' primary factory transitioned to BattleMaster production, limited spare parts availability caused operational numbers to gradually decline despite continued manufacturing runs that introduced various stylistic changes to the chassis profile.

The fall of the Star League marked a turning point for the Catapult. Many operational units accompanied Aleksandr Kerensky on his Exodus, while the Capellan Confederation secured the largest concentration of those remaining in the Inner Sphere. Hollis' factory on Corey briefly resumed production of new frames and spare parts, and the Draconis Combine simultaneously seized a substantial force during their capture of Dieron. The destruction of the Corey facility at the onset of the First Succession War ended renewed production and ensured the Catapult's increasing rarity throughout that devastating conflict. The design became so prized that entire invasions were launched to capture surviving examples, particularly Federated Suns campaigns against the Capellan Confederation.

The Catapult's scarcity began to reverse in 3033 when Yori 'Mech Works was contracted by the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery to restart production on Al Na'ir, initially focusing on the CPLT-K2 variant. This renewed manufacturing capability paved the way for the CPLT-C3, the first BattleMech to mount the newly rediscovered Arrow IV artillery system. Despite a rushed development cycle that reintroduced known deficiencies, the Confederation made excellent use of C3 and Raven tandems, bringing mobile 'Mech-mounted artillery to the forefront of combined-arms doctrine. The far superior O-Bakemono might not exist if not for the C3 paving the way for 'Mech-mounted artillery.

In the years surrounding the Clan Invasion, the Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine retained the largest active Catapult formations, though numerous Periphery realms continued to field centuries-old examples. Variant development continued through the FedCom Civil War, the Jihad, and into the Dark Age, with both Hollis Incorporated on Corey and Yori 'Mech Works on Al Na'ir and later Algedi producing new models. The Catapult's proven adaptability across fire-support, direct-fire, and artillery roles has cemented its legacy as one of the Inner Sphere's most enduring heavy BattleMech platforms.

text.deployment: The Republic's OmniMech conversion serves as a fundamental evolution of the original ComStar concept. Replacing the fixed C3i module with true OmniPod technology and fitting double heat sinks, RAF engineers created a reconfigurable platform capable of adapting to diverse mission requirements. The Prime configuration carries a C3 slave unit and TAG, maintaining the reconnaissance and network-warfare focus of the original design while integrating into the Republic's combined-arms doctrine.

Alternate Configuration A arms the Celerity with a pair of Clan-specification improved one-shot SRM-6 launchers, transforming the drone into a high-speed missile delivery platform. Though the launchers can only fire once, the combination of extreme speed and concentrated short-range firepower makes this configuration effective for spoiling attacks against enemy formations before the missiles are expended.

Alternate Configuration B mounts an Angel ECM suite, dedicating the drone entirely to electronic warfare. This configuration excels at disrupting enemy command networks and sensor systems, and has been employed extensively to interrupt resistance communications across the Fortress Republic's contested territories. The Angel ECM's superior jamming capability compared to standard Guardian systems makes this variant particularly effective at screening advancing Republic formations from enemy sensor coverage.

Alternate Configuration C serves as a dedicated scouting platform, equipped with a remote sensor dispenser and Beagle active probe. This configuration maximizes the Celerity's reconnaissance potential, allowing operators to seed sensor networks across vast areas while the drone's own probe provides real-time detection data. The ability to deploy persistent sensor arrays at extreme speed makes this variant invaluable for establishing early warning networks along threatened borders and contested zones.

Alternate Configuration D mounts a pair of extended-range flamers, providing the drone with an anti-infantry and area-denial capability. Several smaller resistance cells within the Fortress Republic have been eliminated by Celerity drones operating in this configuration, where their extreme speed allows them to close on concealed infantry positions before defenders can react. The flamers' ability to ignite structures and vegetation also makes this variant effective at denying cover to guerrilla forces operating in urban or forested terrain.

Alternate Configuration E represents the most combat-oriented loadout, mounting a Clan-specification extended-range medium laser and an improved heavy medium laser. This combination provides significant firepower for the chassis's tonnage, transforming the disposable drone into a credible direct-combat threat, particularly when operating in coordinated packs. Republic tactical doctrine calls for deploying E-configuration Celeritys in groups of three or more, overwhelming defenders with multiple fast-moving threats that are difficult to track and prioritize simultaneously.

The Primary configuration echoes the proven CN9-D loadout, mounting an LB 10-X autocannon in the right arm, an LRM-10 enhanced with Artemis IV fire control in the left torso, and two ER medium lasers in the center torso with one covering the rear arc. Two tons of ammunition for the autocannon and missile system are stored in the right torso and protected by CASE II. This configuration represents the most familiar Centurion weapons arrangement updated with modern technology, providing balanced firepower across multiple range brackets and serving as the standard baseline from which other configurations depart.

Dropping the rear-firing ER medium laser from the Primary loadout, this configuration replaces the LB 10-X autocannon with a rotary AC/5 fed by three tons of ammunition, dramatically increasing sustained firepower output. The LRM-10 is swapped for an MML-9 retaining the Artemis IV fire control, providing tactical flexibility through the ability to fire both long-range and short-range missile types from a single launcher. The configuration mirrors the CN9-D5's emphasis on high-volume autocannon fire, updated to leverage the OmniMech's pod technology for rapid reconfiguration between engagements.

A more radical departure from the Primary configuration, this loadout removes all standard weaponry in favor of a heavy PPC in the right arm and an MML-7 with Artemis IV fire control in the left torso. A targeting computer in the center torso enhances accuracy for both weapons, while a Guardian ECM suite in the right torso provides electronic warfare capability. Two tons of CASE II-protected missile ammunition and an additional double heat sink round out the pod allocation. The configuration excels at medium to long range engagements while providing electronic protection for the formation.

Retaining the ER medium lasers and LRM-10 from the Primary configuration, this variant replaces the LB 10-X autocannon with a plasma rifle and two tons of ammunition in the right arm. A Guardian ECM suite and C3 slave unit provide electronic warfare and networked targeting capability, while five torso-mounted jump jets grant this configuration the greatest mobility of any standard Centurion OmniMech loadout. The combination of jump capability, electronic countermeasures, and information sharing makes this one of the most tactically versatile configurations, well-suited for reconnaissance-in-force missions and operations requiring rapid repositioning across varied terrain.

Visually distinct from other configurations, this melee-oriented variant mounts a hatchet in the right arm and a medium shield on the left arm, reflecting a close-combat doctrine unusual for the Centurion lineage. Two forward-facing ER medium lasers and an MML-9 with two tons of CASE II-protected ammunition provide ranged firepower, while a rear-facing ER small laser deters pursuit. Four torso-mounted jump jets enhance mobility for closing with opponents, and the shield provides additional protection during the approach, making this configuration particularly effective in urban environments where engagement ranges are short and physical combat is common.

Mounting fewer weapon systems than any other standard configuration, this variant focuses on delivering devastating precision firepower through a Gauss rifle in the right arm with two tons of ammunition. Two ER medium lasers in the center torso provide supplementary firepower at closer ranges. The remaining pod space is dedicated to an Angel ECM suite for advanced electronic warfare capability and a C3 boosted slave for enhanced networked targeting. This configuration transforms the Centurion into a long-range precision striker, leveraging information warfare systems to maximize the effectiveness of each Gauss rifle shot while denying the enemy electronic intelligence about friendly force dispositions.

text.overview: The Cerberus is a ninety-five-ton assault BattleMech produced by LexaTech Industries, introduced in 3054 from the company's facility on Hun Ho in the Draconis Combine. Conceived as LexaTech's bid to create a design worthy of competing with classic Star League-era assault 'Mechs like the King Crab and Atlas, the Cerberus was built around a philosophy of combining heavy long-range firepower with speed unusual for its weight class. The design's massive engine propels the 'Mech to speeds approaching sixty-five kilometers per hour, making it one of the fastest assault 'Mechs in production. LexaTech used the Cerberus to successfully diversify into the conventional heavy BattleMech market during the post-Clan Invasion rearmament period.
text.capabilities:
Firepower appears to have been the sole consideration driving the Cerberus design. For long- and medium-range engagements, it carries two devastating Grizzard Model 200 Gauss rifles, one mounted in each arm. Though such powerful weapons were in limited supply during the design phase, the advantage of possessing such awesome firepower overrode any objections, and with several well-placed shots a Cerberus can cripple virtually any opponent. Supporting these heavy weapons, a quartet of Blankenburg medium pulse lasers lurks behind well-concealed fire doors on the 'Mech's upper torso, sliding away during combat to extend the lasers' field of fire. A favored tactic involves waiting until an unsuspecting foe closes to point-blank range before deploying these close-combat weapons to devastating effect.

The Cerberus achieves its exceptional speed through the massive GM 380 XL engine, but this comes at the price of only eleven tons of Aldis Heavy ferro-fibrous armor protecting the chassis, a meager amount for a ninety-five-ton assault 'Mech. Designers included a pair of rear-firing Sperry Browning machine guns for anti-infantry defense and a head-mounted McArthur anti-missile system to provide protection against missile attacks. The reinforced lower torso and legs provide a strong and steady firing platform, but pilots must exercise caution in close-quarters engagements where the 'Mech's thin armor can be quickly exploited by concentrated fire.
text.deployment: Introduced in the 3120s after LexaTech Industries restored the Hun Ho production facility, this variant is a comprehensive modernization of the Cerberus design for the Dark Age battlefield. Built around an Endo Steel chassis and protected by anti-ballistic armor, this variant retains the twin Gauss rifles that define the design while upgrading the medium pulse lasers to newer models. The machine guns and anti-missile system of the original are removed, reflecting a shift in design philosophy toward streamlined lethality. These changes keep the Cerberus competitive alongside contemporary assault 'Mechs fielded by the rearming Draconis Combine.
text.battleHistory:
The Cerberus was born from LexaTech Industries' ambition to produce a powerful assault 'Mech in the tradition of the classic Star League designs. LexaTech, long recognized as the Draconis Combine's foremost manufacturer of Land-Air 'Mechs at their Irece facility, had lost that plant to Clan Nova Cat during the invasion of 3051. Seeking to rebuild and diversify, the company turned its Hun Ho facility toward developing a new heavy assault design. After more than a year of intensive engineering effort, the Cerberus entered production in 3054.

With the Inner Sphere still reeling from the Clan Invasion, LexaTech found an eager market for their new design. Cashing in on the rearmament frenzy, the company was willing to sell the Cerberus to virtually anyone, Inner Sphere Great Houses, minor nobles, and well-heeled mercenary commands alike. This open sales policy allowed the Cerberus to spread rapidly across the Inner Sphere and beyond. Though the initial enthusiasm prompted by the 'Mech's raw firepower eventually cooled as buyers gained experience with its thin armor protection, demand remained high throughout the Clan Invasion era and into the Civil War period.

The Free Worlds League and Word of Blake both adopted the Cerberus and developed their own modified variant, the MR-5M, which traded one Gauss rifle for improved survivability. The Word of Blake later took this further with the MR-6B modification at Gibson, incorporating their signature improved C3 computer for network-centric warfare. Meanwhile, the straightforward MR-V3 field refit proved popular across factions, with units simply stripping the machine guns to bolster armor protection.

During the Jihad, the Hun Ho facility continued production under Draconis Combine control. By 3079, the plant was operating at approximately ninety percent of its pre-Jihad capacity, having suffered no combat losses, a reflection of the facility's remote location near the Bergen continent's polar region. However, the military drawdowns of the early Republic era saw the plant primarily mothballed, with only limited production of spare parts maintained. The MR-V2 production line fell silent.

The collapse of the HPG network in 3132 prompted the Draconis Combine to reactivate the Hun Ho facility and restore full production capacity. LexaTech introduced the modernized MR-7K in the 3120s, incorporating Endo Steel construction and anti-ballistic armor to keep the venerable design competitive with contemporary assault 'Mechs. The Cerberus continues to serve across the Inner Sphere as a formidable long-range fire support platform, its twin Gauss rifles remaining as fearsome as when the design first rolled off the assembly line on Hun Ho decades earlier.

text.overview:
When the Star League Defense Force departed the Inner Sphere in 2784, they brought several prototype Clints in the original configuration mounting the Armstrong Buster autocannon. These prototypes were placed in a Brian Cache on Circe, where they languished throughout the Exodus Civil War until Clan Snow Raven claimed them following the annihilation of Clan Wolverine and the nuclear attack on their capital of Dehra Dun.

Snow Raven scientists worked to correct the stress problems on the 'Mech's frame caused by the heavier autocannon, and by 2830 had transformed the poorly regarded prototype into a well-armed reconnaissance 'Mech. The design was formally introduced in 2842 and became known as the Clint IIC, serving the Ravens through the Golden Century before production ceased in 2917.
text.capabilities:
The Ravens' key modification was replacing the large Pitban 240 fusion plant with a locally produced Type 81 XL engine. While offering the same output as the Pitban, the Type 81 was much lighter, allowing technicians to reinforce the arm and shoulder skeleton that repeatedly failed on the prototypes. Additional spare mass was used to increase armor protection to seven tons and expand ammunition capacity to four tons.

During the Golden Century, the design was further modified, replacing the Armstrong Buster cannon with a Type KOV LB 10-X autocannon that allowed selectable ammunition loads, and upgrading the lasers to Series 2d extended-range medium variants. All other systems remained as in the original Andoran Industries model, and many retained their SLDF designations. Ironically, the Clint IIC still uses the original Sloane 220 Lockover targeting system, evidence of that component's exceptional quality.

The Clint IIC serves as an effective light 'Mech hunter, capable of ranging far beyond supply lines thanks to its generous ammunition reserves. However, the design retains only ten single heat sinks, limiting sustained fire capability, and its seven tons of standard armor provide adequate but not exceptional protection for a medium 'Mech of its era.
text.deployment: Debuting in 3128 on Noisiel in the Solaris VII arena circuit, this custom variant reverses the typical trend of Clan-modified Inner Sphere machines by starting from a Clan-built frame and incorporating Inner Sphere experimental technology. The designers removed the armor, jump jets, and autocannon from the original Clint IIC chassis, mounting instead a large variable-speed pulse laser and medium re-engineered laser alongside two retained Clan ER medium lasers, all linked to a Clan targeting computer for enhanced accuracy. Ballistic-reinforced armor provides specialized protection against autocannons and missiles commonly encountered in arena combat, though the cramped cockpit and lack of jump capability limit the design's tactical flexibility outside dueling scenarios.
text.battleHistory:
Clan Snow Raven used the Clint IIC extensively during the Golden Century, deploying it in many clashes with other Clans. The most notable engagement was the defense of the Hellgate agrodomes in 2897, where the speed and maneuverability of the Clint IIC provided the Ravens with a significant advantage. However, battlefield inexperience cost them the fight, prompting the Clan to abandon the mining colony to the Steel Vipers only two years later.

With the Ravens' acquisition of OmniMech technology, many of their second-line 'Mechs were relegated to rear-echelon duty, including the Clint IIC. Following a policy of quality rather than quantity, by the late thirtieth century the Ravens faced the choice of decommissioning or mothballing the venerable design. The Blood Spirits' offer in 2977 to trade several of their WarShips for Snow Raven 'Mech surplus came at an opportune time, and most Clint IICs were transferred to the Spirits, becoming part of their Omicron Galaxy.

Following the destruction of several Blood Spirit Galaxies in their battles with Clan Star Adder and Clan Burrock, few Clints remained in Spirit service. The waning fortunes of the Clint IIC were reversed in 3052, when the Snow Ravens built the first new units since production ceased in 2917, seeking to exploit the invading Clans' need for equipment to replace their war losses. Clans Wolf and Ghost Bear acquired the largest numbers of the design, trading resources from the Inner Sphere for manufacturing output. The Ravens have refused to trade the design to either the Steel Vipers or Jade Falcons due to ongoing feuds with those Clans.
